messages:
sanjay: Noticing a sharp rack-hop jitter slice during the 11:30-12:00 batch packing window on us-west-2a. p50 fine, p95 jumps 4-6x for ~3m. Root traces show increased retransmits between rack-8c and rack-8d.

elaine: Saw the alert. Any RDMA QP flaps or port errors in the kernel logs?

sanjay: Logs show repeated QP reset messages and a handful of PMTU ICMP fragments dropped. Example from node gpu-8c-12: 
```
[ 2026-03-17T11:33:12Z ] mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: mlx5_set_qp_state failed (-110) QP 34567
[ 2026-03-17T11:33:12Z ] rdma_cm: cm_id event: CONNECT_ERROR status -110
```

tom_k: That looks like peerlink instability. Are we concurrently doing any MTU/tor config pushes?

nina_ops: We rolled a ToR SR-IOV firmware patch on a subset of racks at 11:20, but rollouts were throttled. Patch notes said "fixed PMTU negotiation" — might be related.

mike_net: I pulled `ethtool -S` and RX partial/frag counters ticked on the 8d side. Also seeing GRO fallback: `gso_max_size` errors. Will attach dumps.

infra-bot: alert: cluster/us-west-2a/gpu-pool latency p95 exceeded threshold (1200ms) for 3m at 2026-03-17T11:33:00Z

elaine: If RDMA QPs are resetting, runtime will stall KV cache access during prefix batching — explains the token-level latency spike. Can we repro by hitting that rack pairing?

sanjay: Running a short synthetic batch run against the affected rack pair now (10k small seqs).

mike_net: While that runs I recommend pinning traffic to non-fragmenting MTU path: `ip route replace ... mtu 9000` on tor-edge as a quick mitigation. Also adding `sysctl net.ipv4.frag_high_thresh` tweak was helpful in a similar incident.

tom_k: Can we avoid live MTU fiddling without full change control? Might cause other flows to fail. Prefer targeted A/B on the afflicted ToRs.

nina_ops: I can limit the firmware rollout set to stop at rack-8d and rollback that switch. Will do a rollback hold and notify ops.

sanjay: Synthetic run shows QP resets correlate with a spike in retransmits at 11:32:45. After we paused firmware rollout, p95 dropped back toward baseline in ~90s.

elaine: Good — that points to the rollout as the likely trigger. Next: create a postmortem patch to add a canary stage that watches RDMA counters before mass rollouts for ToR firmware.

mike_net: Agreed. I'll open a runbook PR with commands to snapshot `rdma` and `ethtool` counters and a quick revert playbook. For now, Nina, keep the rollback and we should throttle any remaining ToR updates in us-west-2a.

nina_ops: Rollback initiated for rack-8d. Pausing the rest. I'll follow up with a granular inventory of switches that pulled the patch.

tom_k: Also worth adding a runtime guard: if p95 > X for >Y seconds, route new batch windows away from the affected rack pair. We can add that to smart routing as a short-term safety net.

sanjay: Filing ticket: INFRA-1298 — "ToR firmware canary + RDMA counter gating + runtime routing fallback". Assigning to @mike_net and @elaine.

infra-bot: ticket INFRA-1298 created and assigned to mike_net, elaine

elaine: Thanks all. Quick notes: do not re-run the firmware rollout until we validate PMTU/fragment handling on canary ToRs.

mike_net: I'll draft the runbook now and share a snippet for the quick checks: 
```
# check RDMA QP errors
sudo cat /sys/class/infiniband/mlx5_0/ports/1/qp_err_counters
# check frag counters
ethtool -S eth0 | egrep 'frag|gso|rx_err'
```

nina_ops: I'll post the rollback confirmation once complete.

sanjay: Closing loop: after rollback, batch windows returned to normal for the last two cycles. Leaving monitoring on for two hours. :white_check_mark:
